title: Home Mortgage Loans: adjustable-rate caps and rate change notice period
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: adjustable-rate caps and rate change notice period

This document states, for each Home Mortgage Loans program, the largest rate change allowed at the first adjustment and at each later adjustment, the largest total increase over the start rate, and how many days before the first payment at a new rate the change notice is sent.

## Caps by program

| Program | Largest change at the first adjustment (%) | Largest change at each later adjustment (%) | Largest total increase over the start rate (%) | Change notice sent before the first payment at the new rate (calendar days) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FHA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| VA 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| Conventional 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| Conventional 15-Year Fixed Mortgage | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |
| 7/6 SOFR Adjustable-Rate Mortgage | 5.00 | 1.00 | 5.00 | 60 |
| Jumbo 30-Year Fixed Mortgage | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable | Not applicable |

"Not applicable" means the program sets no cap or notice period. Only the 7/6 SOFR Adjustable-Rate Mortgage sets them.

## Reading the caps of the 7/6 SOFR Adjustable-Rate Mortgage

| Cap | Figure | What it limits |
|---|---|---|
| First-adjustment cap | 5.00 | The size of the rate change at the first adjustment |
| Periodic cap | 1.00 | The size of the rate change at each adjustment after the first |
| Lifetime cap | 5.00 | The total increase over the start rate |
| Notice period | 60 calendar days | How far ahead of the first payment at the new rate the change notice is sent |

## Worked example (hypothetical start rate)

For a 7/6 SOFR Adjustable-Rate Mortgage loan with a hypothetical start rate of 6.000 percent, the lifetime cap of 5.00 means the rate may rise by no more than 5.00 percentage points over 6.000, so the highest rate the lifetime cap allows is 11.000 percent.

## Basis Q&A

- **Is the first-adjustment cap the same as the later caps?** No. The first adjustment may change the rate by up to 5.00 percentage points; each later adjustment by up to 1.00.
